analysis.statement:
`main` — persistent demand-aware fan-in trace evaluator

Implement one complete Rust program containing `fn main()`. Use only the Rust standard library.

There are `N` one-shot producers and queue tickets `0..N-1`. Version `0` has producer and consumer indices `p=c=0`, demand `d=0`, all producers unreserved, and all slots unpublished. Operation `i` creates version `i` from an earlier version `b`; versions may branch.

Operations:

* `R b s`: reserve producer `s`. It receives ticket `p`, then `p` increases by one.
* `W b s E`: publish producer `s` as a value-less completion.
* `W b s V x`: publish signed 64-bit value `x`.
* `D b k`: add `k` units of value demand.
* `P b`: drain the queue.

Reservations and publications leave `c,d` unchanged. `D` leaves `p,c` unchanged. Every input is valid: `0 <= b < i`; reservations occur only for an unreserved producer with `p<N`; publications occur only once for a reserved producer. Producer IDs are `1..N`. Along every version ancestry, demand never exceeds `10^18`.

A drain examines tickets in increasing order starting at `c` and repeats:

* An unpublished slot stops draining.

time_memory_risks: numeric bounds too large for naive loops or arrays
n up to ~1e5–5e5; need near-linear work

plan.approach: Use a persistent segment tree over the ticket range [0,N). Each node stores the state of a slot: none, completion, or value. For each operation we clone the root of the previous version and apply the change. Reservations and publications modify the tree at a single index. Demand and consumer index are stored per version. Drain operation walks the tree from the current consumer index, collecting values while demand>0. Since N≤150k, the tree depth is ≤18, so each update and query is O(logN).
data_structures: persistent segment tree node { left, right, state }
plan.complexity_target: O((Q+N) log N) time, O((Q+N) log N) memory
traps_to_handle: huge demand values up to 1e18 – use 128-bit integers for sums
persistent updates must not clone entire tree – only O(logN) nodes
drain must stop correctly when encountering unpublished slot or demand zero
status determination after drain must use updated p,c,d
plan.return_shape: string of tokens separated by spaces and newlines
test_ideas: 1. Simple case N=1, single reservation, publication, demand, drain – check output tokens
2. Branching: create two versions from same base, perform different operations, drain each – ensure isolation
3. Large demand: add 1e18 demand, publish value, drain – verify value consumed and demand decremented
4. Backpressure: publish value but no demand, drain – status should be BACKPRESSURE
5. Blocked: publish completion, no value, drain – status BLOCKED if next slot unpublished
6. Complete: all tickets consumed and p=c=N – status COMPLETE
